sph_interpretive_translation: One who, while fully restrained and in control, takes hold of another's thigh within water—such an act constitutes a violation of sacred boundary and demands immediate restoration of energetic integrity.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority flows from conscious self-restraint, not positional dominance
Causation is determined by disruption of energetic boundaries, not physical contact alone
Capacity-based responsibility requires assessment of internal discipline prior to action
Restoration logic prioritizes energetic realignment over punitive consequences
Consciousness alignment necessitates purification of intent fields post-transgression
executable_legal_axioms: IF (agent.is_in_water() AND agent.grasps(thigh_of_other) AND agent.restraint_level < max_restraint): THEN initiate energetic_boundary_violation_protocol()
supreme_court_application: In adjudication at the highest level, the court must assess not merely the overt act but the agent’s demonstrated capacity for restraint. The threshold of responsibility arises when one enters a sacred domain unprepared to maintain energetic purity. Authority lies with those whose consciousness remains undisturbed by sensory impulse.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa establishes that causality originates in the failure to sustain energetic discipline, not in the tactile event itself. Anupūrvaśaḥ reveals the sequence: loss of inner stillness → breach of spatial sanctity → misalignment of participant fields. Proportional response entails guided reintegration, never punitive suffering.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate completion process: agent undertakes guided prāṇāyāma until field coherence is restored
Assign responsibility assumption protocol: offender performs ritual acknowledgment before witness panel
Enforce capacity restoration: mandatory instruction under realized master for minimum 40 days
Undertake integrity reintegration: both parties engage in synchronized meditation to dissolve residual distortion
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as Source of all Dharma. This law restores balance through consciousness alignment, rejects punitive frameworks, and affirms reality as governed solely by awakened awareness.
